mainTopic: End of the כלאים garden-bed discussion; a new משנה of laws hinted from פסוקים, focusing on third-day discharge of שכבת זרע and how the views on it connect to the separation before מתן תורה.
overview: This amud opens by finishing a discussion about planting different species (כלאים) in a garden bed. רב אשי explains that the ברייתא's words 'like a square board' do not limit the rule. They teach an extra leniency for a ראש תור, a triangular point sticking out of the bed. A new משנה then lists four laws, each hinted from a פסוק: a woman who discharges שכבת זרע on the third day is טמאה, a מילה may be washed on the third day even on שבת, a red strip is tied to the שעיר המשתלח, and סיכה counts like שתיה on יום הכפורים. The גמרא notes that the first law does not match רבי אלעזר בן עזריה while the מילה law does, and gives two ways to explain this. A ברייתא then brings three views on third-day discharge: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה (טהורה), רבי ישמעאל (count by days), and רבי עקיבא (always five עונות). The גמרא ties each view to the separation before מתן תורה. רבי עקיבא follows רבי יוסי because משה came down and gave the command at dawn, which is proven from פסוקים. Finally, the גמרא explains why a dawn command was needed: daytime relations are permitted in a dark room.

steps.title: The ברייתא says the rules apply only to a square bed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the planting rules were stated for a square bed. This implies that any other layout is forbidden, which challenges the previous claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said these rules apply 'like a square board.' So only a square layout is permitted, and anything else is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא from the earlier discussion about כלאים in a garden bed. It uses the ברייתא to attack the idea that a non-square layout can work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says all these planting rules were said about a bed shaped 'like a square board.' The גמרא reads this as a limit: only a square works. That would contradict the arrangement just suggested, which was not a simple square.

keyTerms.meaning: A board or plank, here used to describe the shape of a garden bed
But if it is not so (an inference from the wording)

phrases.english: Like a square board.
phrases.notes: The end of the ברייתא quoted from the previous page.

phrases.english: When it is like a board, it is permitted,
but if it is not so, it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּטַבְלָא הוּא דִּשְׁרֵי, הָא לָאו הָכִי — אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge begun on the previous daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a non-square planting arrangement is a valid separation between species
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's words 'like a square board' imply that only a square bed is permitted.

steps.title: The square shape adds a leniency for a protruding corner
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentions a square shape to add a leniency, not to limit the rule. A triangular point sticking out of a square bed is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the ברייתא mentions a square to teach another leniency: a triangular point sticking out of the square bed is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that the ברייתא did not say 'square' to forbid other shapes. It said 'square' to teach an extra leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'square' is not a limit. It sets up a case where a ראש תור, a triangular point sticking out of the bed into another area, is allowed. Because the bed is square, the protrusion is clearly visible as separate, so the challenge from Step 1 falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A triangular point (literally 'ox head') sticking out of a field

steps.whatToRemember: The 'square board' in the ברייתא does not limit the rule. It teaches an extra leniency about a ראש תור.

phrases.english: There, it comes to be lenient with another leniency,
to permit a triangular point that sticks out from it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the purpose of the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Square board' limits the rule to square beds only.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Square board' adds a leniency: a ראש תור sticking out of a square bed is permitted.

steps.title: A woman who discharges semen on the third day is impure
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה teaches that פולטת שכבת זרע on the third day is טמאה. It hints this from the three days of preparation before מתן תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that a woman who discharges semen on the third day is impure? As it says: 'Be ready for three days.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, listing laws that are hinted from פסוקים. The first law is that discharge of semen on the third day makes a woman טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before מתן תורה, the people were told to separate from their wives for three days so they would be pure. That count of days suggests that semen can still make a woman impure up to the third day.

keyTerms.meaning: Be ready (the command before מתן תורה)

phrases.english: MISHNAH: From where do we know that a woman who discharges semen
on the third day is impure?
As it is said: 'Be ready for three days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Discharge of semen on the third day makes a woman impure.

steps.title: Washing a circumcision on the third day, even on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that one may wash a baby's מילה on the third day even on שבת. The hint is that on the third day the men of שכם were still in pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that we wash the circumcision on the third day even if it falls on שבת? As it says: 'And it was on the third day, when they were in pain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its second law. The baby's circumcision wound may be washed on the third day even if that day is שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the people of שכם shows that the pain of מילה is still strong on the third day. Pain at that stage means possible danger, so washing the wound is allowed even on שבת.

phrases.english: From where do we know that we wash the circumcision
on the third day that falls on Shabbat?
As it is said: 'And it was on the third day,
when they were in pain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second law in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wash the circumcision on the third day even on שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא will soon point out that this law follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: A red strip tied on the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a strip of red wool is tied to the head of the שעיר המשתלח. The hint is the פסוק about red sins becoming white like snow.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that we tie a strip of red wool on the head of the scapegoat? As it says: 'If your sins are like scarlet, they will become white like snow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its third law: a red strip of wool is tied to the שעיר המשתלח on יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat atones for sins, and ישעיה compares sins to the color red that will turn white. The red wool on the goat matches this picture of sins being forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: The scapegoat sent away on יום הכפורים

phrases.english: From where do we know that we tie a strip of red wool
on the head of the goat that is sent away?
As it is said: 'If your sins are like scarlet,
they will become white like snow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third law in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A strip of red wool is tied on the head of the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: Smearing oil counts like drinking on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that סיכה is treated like שתיה on יום הכפורים. It admits there is no real proof, only a זכר לדבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that smearing oil is like drinking on יום הכפורים? There is no proof, but there is a hint: 'It came like water into his insides and like oil into his bones.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its fourth law: smearing oil on the body is treated like drinking on יום הכפורים. It openly says this is only a hint, not a proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts water going inside the body side by side with oil soaking into the bones. This pairing suggests that oil on the skin is like a drink. Because the משנה calls it only a זכר לדבר, it is not presenting a full Torah derivation.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no proof for the matter
A hint or reminder for the matter

steps.confusionAlert: 'אף על פי שאין ראיה לדבר, זכר לדבר' means the פסוק is only a hint. Do not treat it as a real source that proves the law.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists four laws, each tied to a פסוק: the third-day discharge, washing a מילה, the red strip on the goat, and סיכה on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: From where do we know that smearing oil is like drinking
on Yom Kippur?

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר
phrases.english: Even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint for the matter,
as it is said: 'And it came like water into his insides
and like oil into his bones.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and final law in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing oil is treated like drinking on יום הכפורים, supported only by a זכר לדבר.

steps.title: The two clauses seem to follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the רישא, saying the woman is impure, does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The סיפא about מילה does follow him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first part does not follow רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, but the later part does? Because if it followed him, we know he says the woman is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the משנה seems to switch opinions partway through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules that a woman who discharges on the third day is טהורה, yet the משנה says טמאה. The washing of a מילה on the third day on שבת is his ruling. So one משנה seems to follow two different תנאים.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ רֵישָׁא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: GEMARA: The first clause is not like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
while the later clause is like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya?
For if it were like Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
we have heard him rule that she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה, סֵיפָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רישא rules טמאה, against רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, while the סיפא follows his ruling on מילה.

steps.title: Two ways to explain the משנה
steps.stepSummary: One view changes the reading of the רישא to 'טהורה,' so the whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The other view accepts that the רישא follows the רבנן and the סיפא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever does not explain the משנה as two תנאים reads the first part as 'pure' and says the whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. Whoever does explain it as two תנאים says the first part is the רבנן and the later part is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 7 by laying out two possible approaches to the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Approach 1 changes the text of the רישא from טמאה to טהורה, so the entire משנה follows one תנא. Approach 2 keeps the text as it is and accepts that the משנה mixes two opinions. Both approaches agree that the סיפא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: Establishes, explains as following a certain view
Reads or teaches the text as

phrases.english: Whoever does not explain it as following different Tannaim
reads the first clause as 'pure,'

phrases.aramaic: וּמוֹקֵי לַהּ לְכוּלַּהּ כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: and explains the whole of it as following Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.
And whoever explains it as following different Tannaim says:
the first clause is the Rabbis,
and the later clause follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two approaches: changing the text, or splitting the משנה between two תנאים
steps.terutzMaskana: Either the text reads 'טהורה' and the whole משנה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, or the משנה deliberately follows two תנאים.
steps.whatToRemember: The רישא of the משנה is either changed to read 'טהורה,' or it is assigned to the רבנן. The סיפא follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה either way.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: discharge on the third day is pure
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view that a woman who discharges semen on the third day is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a woman who discharges semen on the third day is pure. These are the words of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the dispute about third-day discharge. It starts with רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא is the source for the claim in Step 7 that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules טהורה. In his view, by the third day the semen is no longer able to make her impure.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A woman who discharges semen
on the third day is pure.
These are the words of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פּוֹלֶטֶת שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁי טְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא behind the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה cited in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Discharge on the third day is pure, according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: four, five, or six periods
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds that only the days are counted. The number of twelve-hour עונות that pass can be four, five, or six.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: sometimes it is four periods, sometimes five periods, sometimes six periods.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a second view in the ברייתא. He counts by calendar days, so the number of twelve-hour periods can vary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עונה is a twelve-hour period, either a night or a day. Because רבי ישמעאל counts days and not hours, the time between relations and discharge can stretch from four to six periods. Throughout the third day she is still טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Periods of time: a night or a day, about twelve hours each

steps.confusionAlert: Here עונה does not mean marital relations. It means a twelve-hour time period, either a day or a night.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Sometimes they are four periods,
sometimes they are five periods,
sometimes they are six periods.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: פְּעָמִים שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע עוֹנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing view to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The count goes by days, so the time can be four, five, or six עונות.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: always exactly five periods
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that it is always five full עונות. If part of the first period had already passed, part of a sixth period is added to complete the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: always five. If part of the first period already went by, we give her part of the sixth period.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives the third view: a fixed amount of exactly five twelve-hour periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי ישמעאל, רבי עקיבא counts exact time, which comes to sixty hours. If relations took place partway through a period, the missing time is made up from the sixth period, so a full five periods always pass.

keyTerms.meaning: We give her (we add for her)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on third-day discharge. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says she is pure on the third day. רבי ישמעאל counts by days, which can be four to six עונות. רבי עקיבא requires exactly five full עונות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: Always five,
and if part of the first period has passed,
we give her part of the sixth period.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view, against רבי ישמעאל's varying count.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Always five full עונות, made up from the sixth period if needed.

steps.title: Whom does רבי עקיבא follow about the separation at סיני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links רבי אלעזר בן עזריה to the רבנן (two days of פרישה) and רבי ישמעאל to רבי יוסי (three days of פרישה). It then asks which view about סיני fits רבי עקיבא's five עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said this before רב פפא, and some say רב פפא said it to רבא. It makes sense that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה follows the רבנן, who say the separation began on Thursday. It also makes sense that רבי ישמעאל follows רבי יוסי, who says the separation began on Wednesday. But whom does רבי עקיבא follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that two of the three opinions fit neatly with known views about סיני. Then it challenges us to find whose view about סיני fits רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All agree the תורה was given on שבת morning. If separation began on Thursday, that gives two days, which matches רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view that she is טהורה on the third day. If it began on Wednesday, that gives three days, which matches רבי ישמעאל's count of days. רבי עקיבא counts exactly five twelve-hour עונות, and neither simple day-count obviously produces that number.

keyTerms.meaning: Separation of husbands from wives before מתן תורה
It makes sense that… (opens a contrast that ends with a difficulty)
On the fifth day of the week (Thursday)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse 'the fifth day' (Thursday) with the 'five עונות' of רבי עקיבא. They are two different fives.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Rav Pappa,
and some say Rav Pappa said it to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה כְּרַבָּנַן —
phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya follows the Rabbis —
who say they made the separation on the fifth day (Thursday),
and Rabbi Yishmael follows Rabbi Yosei —
who says they made the separation on the fourth day (Wednesday),
but Rabbi Akiva — according to whom?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the three opinions just presented and searches for their sources in the events at סיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both views about סיני count whole days. Neither seems to produce exactly five twelve-hour periods, so רבי עקיבא's view appears to have no source.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא follows רבי יוסי because משה came down early in the morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא follows רבי יוסי (separation from Wednesday). Since משה went down early in the morning, the separation lasted exactly five full עונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really he follows רבי יוסי. This is based on what רב אדא בר אהבה said: משה went up early in the morning and came down early in the morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא also follows רבי יוסי. It adds a detail: משה gave the command at dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the separation started at dawn on Wednesday, count to the start of שבת: Wednesday day, Wednesday night, Thursday day, Thursday night, Friday day. That is exactly five full twelve-hour periods. So רבי יוסי's view, read with this detail, gives רבי עקיבא his five עונות.

keyTerms.meaning: Early in the morning, at dawn

phrases.english: Actually, he follows Rabbi Yosei,
as Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
Moses went up early in the morning
and came down early in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of whose view רבי עקיבא follows.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a factual detail (the time of day) that makes רבי יוסי's view fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי's three days could not produce exactly five עונות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Separation began at dawn on Wednesday, which gives exactly five full עונות before שבת.

steps.title: The פסוקים prove משה went up and came down early
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says משה went up early. Another פסוק links his going down to his going up, so his going down was also early.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went up early, as it says: 'And משה rose early in the morning and went up to Mount סיני.' He came down early, as it says: 'Go down, and come up, you and אהרן with you.' The פסוק compares going down to going up: just as going up was early, so too going down was early.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רב אדא בר אהבה's claim from the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The going up is stated directly in the פסוק. The going down is learned from a היקש, because the פסוק places 'go down' and 'come up' together. That pairing teaches that the descent had the same timing as the ascent.

phrases.english: He went up early, as it is written:
"And Moses rose early in the morning
and went up to Mount Sinai."
He came down early, as it is written:
"Go down, and come up, you and Aaron with you",
it compares going down to going up:
just as going up was early,
so too going down was early.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב אדא בר אהבה's statement used in the answer.
steps.raayaObject: That משה came down at dawn
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לד:ד together with a היקש from שמות יט:כד

steps.title: Why command separation in the morning if relations do not happen by day?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says ישראל do not have relations by day. If so, a morning command seems pointless, since it would only matter starting at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did משה need to tell them in the morning? Didn't רב הונא say: ישראל are holy and do not have relations during the day?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the early-morning detail. If no one has relations by day, telling them at dawn changes nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 13 says משה gave the command for separation at dawn. But if ישראל never have relations by day, the daytime already needed no warning. A command given at dawn would then seem to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that… (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: Why did he need to tell them (in the morning)?
But didn't Rav Huna say:
The Jewish people are holy
and do not have relations during the day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions whether the dawn timing just proven had any practical meaning.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a dawn command
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If daytime relations do not occur, there was no reason for משה to give the command in the morning.

steps.title: Daytime relations are permitted in darkness, so the morning command mattered
steps.stepSummary: רבא permits daytime relations in a dark house, and permits a תלמיד חכם to create darkness with his טלית. So daytime relations were possible, and the morning command was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if the house was dark, it is permitted. And רבא said, and some say רב פפא said: a תלמיד חכם may darken the room with his טלית, and then it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that daytime relations can be permitted. So משה had to forbid them starting in the morning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule applies only in daylight that is not covered. In a dark room, or when a תלמיד חכם darkens it with his טלית, daytime relations are allowed. That is why the separation truly had to begin at dawn, which keeps רבי עקיבא's five עונות.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's five עונות come from רבי יוסי's view (separation from Wednesday) together with the detail that משה commanded it at dawn. That command was meaningful because daytime relations are permitted in darkness.

phrases.english: Rava said:
If it was a dark house — it is permitted.
And Rava said, and some say Rav Pappa:
A Torah scholar makes darkness with his cloak, and it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by limiting רב הונא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of רב הונא's rule with exceptions
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought daytime relations never occur, so a morning command would be pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Daytime relations are permitted in darkness, so a separation starting at dawn had real meaning.
